value.text: Traveller, you look half drowned yourself. Sit a moment. I am Maren, the healer here.
Since the flood the bell in the old belfry has been silent, and the marsh has gone dark and hungry.
Will you go to the belfry?

options.text: How do I cross the marsh?
Where would I find a lantern?

value.text: Warden Hale keeps the causeway gate and lets no one into Blackmere without a light. Past it, Odd's ferry, or the old punt by the jetty.
Bram sells them at the inn. There was one in the barn once. And a clever hand can make one at the tinker's bench: an oil flask, and dried herbs for a wick.
Then go with care. The marsh keeps what it takes.
The shrine is lit? I felt it tonight, like a held breath let go.
Find a lantern, then the causeway. The bell is waiting.
The bell rang. Hollowmere can sleep again. Thank you, traveller.
Did you ever hear the bell? Gran says it rang every dusk before the flood.
It fell in the marsh, by the dead willow. Hale will not let me look.
Gran says you light the shrine lanterns the way the sun walks: from the willow in the west to the water in the east.
The belfry? I ferry no strangers over that water. Light the sunken shrine, west to east, and we will talk. Or patch the old punt yourself; it wants pitch from an oil flask.
You lit the old shrine. My mother tended it. I owe you a crossing.
The black water is calm tonight.
I will be here. The water is patient.
